source: https://code4rena.com/reports/<contest>, each repo at the commit the report links
how_labelled: By hand from the reports and the source, 2026-09-19, before any lens was run on this corpus. Every High and Medium finding in every report was classified: either one of the four shapes Quorum's lens pairs look for (reentrancy, unguarded-state-write, unsafe-math, accounting-mismatch) or the category of bug it actually is. A target names the one function where the fix belongs. Contests whose protocol appears in the maintainer's own audit-practice archive were excluded before anything was read, so nothing here was seen during that work. Non-Solidity contests (Rust, Cairo) and reports that link no source were dropped at collection time.
excluded: tests, mocks, harnesses, scripts, interfaces, dependencies (lib/, node_modules/) and build output

findings.title: The calculation of totalAssets() could be wrong if operatorFeeAmount > 0, this can cause potential loss for the new depositors
findings.why: totalAssets() counts the WRON sitting in the vault as the operator fee without subtracting operatorFeeAmount, so share price is inflated then drops when fetchOperatorFee() pays out; operatorFeeAmount IS zeroed on payout (line 124), so this is a wrong share-price formula, not a never-decremented credit.

findings.title: User can earn rewards by frontrunning the new rewards accumulation in Ron staking without actually delegating his tokens
findings.why: The attack is depositing in the block before the Ronin staking period rolls over so getTotalRewards() jumps right after minting shares; no external call ordering, no unchecked math and no missing access control is involved, the fix is a deposit-time lock or fee.

findings.title: Operators are unable to perform any actions due to incorrect modifier implementation
findings.why: The modifier `if (msg.sender != owner() || operator[msg.sender]) revert` uses || and a non-negated operator check, which makes access control stricter (operators locked out), not missing, so it is the opposite of an unguarded state write.

findings.title: Cross-chain signature replay attack due to user-supplied domainSeparator and missing deadline check
findings.why: _verifySig builds the EIP-712 digest from a caller-supplied `domainSeparator` argument instead of computing it from block.chainid, so a signature is valid on every chain; this is a signature-domain flaw, not a reentrancy, unguarded write, wrapping arithmetic or double-credit balance.

findings.title: Lack of deadline check in forwarded request
findings.why: The ForwardRequest struct carries no deadline and execute() never compares block.timestamp against one, so a signed request stays executable forever — a signature-expiry gap, with no external-call reordering, missing access control, overflow or unreduced balance involved.

findings.title: Missing signature duplication check in the submitCheckpoint function
findings.why: validateActiveQuorumSignatures sums getTotalPowerOfValidators(signatories) without deduplicating the signatories array, so one validator's weight is counted repeatedly - a signature-verification flaw, not a reentrancy, access-control, wrapping-arithmetic or unreduced-balance shape.

findings.title: Xnet call messages with value > 0 lead to inflated circulating supply of child subnet
findings.why: commitTopDownMsg credits subnet.circSupply += crossMessage.value for Call messages, but execBottomUpMsgs skips them in totalValue because of `if (msgs[i].kind != IpcMsgKind.Call)`, so that credit is never debited and the same circSupply can back repeated payouts out of the gateway.

findings.title: Reliance on incorrect hash in IpcContract.sol leads to permanent fund loss and receipt message execution failure
findings.why: performIpcCall keys inflightMsgs by envelope.toHash() while the receipt carries toTracingId(), two different keccak preimages, so the lookup misses - a wrong-identifier logic bug with no external-call ordering, access-control, wrapping or unreduced-balance element.

findings.title: An attacker can overflow the count of messages in a bottom up message batch leading to bottom up checkpoint execution failure and halting
findings.why: commitBottomUpMsg calls storeBottomUpMsgBatch on an already-populated batch at block.number so the batch exceeds maxMsgsPerBottomUpBatch and ensureValidCheckpoint permanently reverts; this is an unbounded-growth denial of service, not arithmetic wrapping (pragma ^0.8.23, the only unchecked block is the loop counter).

findings.title: Incorrect supply fund transferral in function leave() can be exploited to drain locked collateral source funds in subnet actor contract
findings.why: leave() refunds the genesis balance with s.collateralSource.transferFunds instead of s.supplySource.transferFunds - the wrong asset is paid out, and the genesisBalance storage entry IS deleted first, so it is a wrong-asset logic bug rather than an unreduced-balance accounting mismatch.

findings.title: Reentrancy in function leave() leads to halting of bottom up checkpoints
findings.why: leave() performs s.collateralSource.transferFunds (a native `recipient.call{value:}`) before the LibStaking.withdrawWithConfirm state write, and the attacker re-enters through stake(), which carries no nonReentrant modifier, so leave()'s own guard does not stop it; the fix is to reorder the call inside leave().

findings.title: Incorrect loop indexing in LibAddressStakingReleases.compact() leads to unprocessed pending releases
findings.why: compact() compares the absolute cursor `i = self.startIdx` against the relative count `self.length` in `while (i < length)`, so the loop stops running - a wrong loop bound, with no wrapping arithmetic (pragma ^0.8.23 and the unchecked block only holds ++i/--newLength).

findings.title: Permissionless creation of new subnets under gateway will lead to gateway actor fund draining
findings.why: register() is external payable with no modifier and no caller check, yet writes gateway-wide privileged state (subnet.stake, subnet.circSupply, s.subnetKeys, s.totalSubnets) that governs payouts from the shared gateway treasury; the recommended fix is exactly an access-control check on msg.sender.

findings.title: Cross msg recipient can block checkpoint submission
findings.why: the `target.call{value: value}(data)` in functionCallWithValue copies unbounded returndata into memory, letting a malicious recipient burn all gas (returndata bomb); the fix is a bounded/ExcessivelySafeCall, not reordering a state write or adding a guard.

findings.title: Functions withdrawWithConfirm and depositWithConfirm incorrectly update genesisValidators state
findings.why: depositWithConfirm only pushes a new genesisValidators entry when !alreadyValidator and never refreshes an existing validator's weight (and withdrawWithConfirm never removes one), a stale-bookkeeping logic bug with no payout, external call, or wrapping arithmetic involved.

findings.title: Refunds to EOAs on unsuccessful cross-chain messages fail, leaving users' funds stuck in the gateway
findings.why: execute() routes Result (refund) messages through supplySource.performCall, whose functionCallWithValue reverts with InvalidSubnetActor when !isContract(target), so an EOA refund path is simply missing - a missing branch, not a guard, access-control, wrapping or unreduced-balance issue.

findings.title: Missing value validation in cross message handler allows unbacked fund transfer
findings.why: register() makes two independent lock() calls that each only `require(msg.value >= value)`, with no aggregate check that msg.value covers genesisCircSupply + collateral - a missing input validation, and the credit IS written once per call rather than an unreduced balance being drained twice.

findings.title: Malicious validators can flood stake/unstake requests to DoS confirmChange preventing other validators from claiming their collateral
findings.why: unstake() accepts any non-zero amount (only `if (amount == 0) revert CannotReleaseZero()`), so 1-wei requests inflate the changeSet loop in LibStaking.confirmChange until it runs out of gas; the fix is a minimum amount, a griefing/DoS shape.

findings.title: Unauthorized reallocation in NudgeCampaign::handleReallocation and reward disruption vulnerability in NudgeCampaign::invalidateParticipations
findings.why: invalidateParticipations subtracts only participation.rewardAmount from pendingRewards and never returns the fee portion to the claimable pool, permanently shrinking claimableRewardAmount() rather than letting one credit be paid out twice.

findings.title: Anyone can DOS handleReallocation over and over
findings.why: The caller gate `factory.hasRole(factory.SWAP_CALLER_ROLE(), msg.sender)` depends on a role the LiFi Executor can be made to renounce by anyone, a griefing DoS on the entry point rather than reentrancy, wrapping math, or a privileged write left unguarded.

findings.title: All reallocate cross-chain token and rewards will be lost for the users using the account abstraction wallet
findings.why: `_transfer(toToken, userAddress, amountReceived)` sends the destination-chain tokens to the source-chain address, which differs for smart-contract wallets across chains; the fix is a destination recipient parameter, not a guard, reorder, or arithmetic change.

findings.title: Not verifying that transaction initiator is the actual participator allows malicious user to allocate full reward as Uniswap V2 pool
findings.why: handleReallocation accepts an arbitrary `userAddress` with no check that it initiated the swap, so a flash-swapped Uniswap pool can be registered as participant; the writes to pendingRewards/participations are per-participation, not privileged state left unguarded.

findings.title: The current implementation is incompatible with WBTC as collateral token
findings.why: This is an 8-vs-18 decimals mismatch against WBTC (COLL_GAS_COMPENSATION_CAP = 2 ether, 8-decimal _collToLiquidate compared to an 18-decimal maxSeizedColl, stake*L_coll/1e18 truncating to zero), which is wrong-scale math and not wrapping arithmetic - pragma is 0.8.24 with no unchecked block - and it is unlocatable because the report spans _getCollGasCompensation (L360), _getCollPenaltyAndSurplus (L421), _getLatestTroveData (L989) and _redistributeDebtAndColl (L1133) and states the fix is a system-wide review rather than one function.

findings.title: Non-whitelisted owner can also hold/own a troveNFT
findings.why: The whitelist check exists in BorrowerOperations.openTrove but is bypassed by a plain ERC721 transfer, so it is a missing-validation bug rather than reentrancy, missing access control on a privileged setter, wrapping arithmetic or an unreduced balance; it is unlocatable because the recommended fix is to add a transferFrom/_update override that does not exist in contracts/src/TroveNFT.sol at this commit (that file defines only tokenURI, mint, burn and _requireCallerIsTroveManager).

findings.title: Buffer Silently Locks Staked HYPE in Contract Without Using Them For Withdrawals Or Providing A Way To Be Pulled Out Or Moved To L1
findings.why: cancelWithdrawal never restores the hypeBuffer that _withdrawFromValidator decremented, so HYPE is stranded rather than double-paid against a never-reduced credit, and no external call precedes an exploitable write.

findings.title: Users Who Queue Withdrawal Before A Slashing Event Disadvantage Users Who Queue After And Eventually Leads To Loss Of Funds For Them
findings.why: The ratio Math.mulDiv(totalHYPE, 1e18, totalKHYPESupply) ignores already-queued withdrawals so slashing losses are not shared, a design/accounting policy flaw with no wrapping arithmetic, external-call ordering, or unguarded privileged write.

findings.title: Mishandling of receiving HYPE in the StakingManager, user can't confirm withdrawal and inflate the exchange ratio
findings.why: receive() unconditionally calls stake(), so HYPE returned from HyperCore is re-staked instead of reserved for withdrawals; the fix is a sender check inside receive(), not a reorder or guard against reentrancy.

findings.title: Incorrect Balance Check in Validator Redelegation Process May Block Legitimate Rebalancing Operations
findings.why: The require(address(this).balance >= amount) check validates an EVM balance for funds that live on HyperCore, a wrong precondition that blocks execution rather than any wrapping math, missing access control, or double payout.

findings.title: Missing withdrawal pause check in confirmWithdrawal allows bypassing withdrawal restrictions
findings.why: confirmWithdrawal lacks the whenWithdrawalNotPaused modifier, but it writes only the caller's own withdrawal request rather than privileged state such as an owner, fee, or pause flag, so it is not an unguarded-state-write.

findings.title: Inconsistent State Restoration in cancelWithdrawal Function
findings.why: cancelWithdrawal restores neither hypeBuffer nor the queued _pendingWithdrawals entry, leaving stale bookkeeping; nothing is paid twice against an un-decremented credit and there is no external call before a state write.

findings.title: Processing all withdrawals before all deposits can cause some deposit to not be delegated in processL1Operations
findings.why: processL1Operations calls _processL1Withdrawals before _processL1Deposits so L1 staking balance is consumed first and some deposits fail to delegate, a sequencing/business-logic flaw with no wrapping arithmetic or unguarded privileged write.

findings.title: Attacker can partially DoS L1 operations in StakingManager by making huge number of deposits
findings.why: The unbounded `delete _pendingDeposits` at the end of _processL1Deposits can exceed the block gas limit after a spam of small stakes, which is a gas-griefing DoS rather than any of the four value-flow bug shapes.

findings.title: Lack of access control in AgentNftV2::addValidator() enables unauthorized validator injection and causes reward accounting inconsistencies
findings.why: addValidator() is `public` with no role modifier and writes protocol-level registry state (_validatorsMap/_validators push and _baseValidatorScore) for any virtualId an attacker names; the recommended fix is literally adding onlyRole to that function.

findings.title: Anybody can control a user's delegate by calling AgentVeToken.stake() with 1 wei
findings.why: stake() is externally callable by anyone and executes `_delegate(receiver, delegatee)` writing the voting-power delegation of an arbitrary third-party `receiver` with no check that the caller is that receiver.

findings.title: Public ServiceNft::updateImpact call leads to cascading issue
findings.why: updateImpact() is declared `public` with no modifier and writes _impacts[proposalId]/_impacts[datasetId] and _maturities, the scoring state that AgentRewardV2 and Minter read to size payouts; the fix is to make it internal.

findings.title: Public ContributionNft::mint leads to cascading issues / loss of funds
findings.why: mint() does gate the caller (`require(msg.sender == personaDAO.proposalProposer(proposalId))`), so the defect is that coreId/parentId/isModel_/datasetId arguments are never validated against the proposal, i.e. unvalidated input rather than a missing access check.

findings.title: ValidatorRegistry::validatorScore/getPastValidatorScore allows validator to earn full rewards without actually engaging with the protocol
findings.why: _initValidatorScore seeds _baseValidatorScore to _getMaxScore(virtualId) (= totalProposals), so a brand new validator scores 100% uptime; the flaw is the chosen participation formula, not wrapping arithmetic or a missing caller check.

findings.title: Missing prevAgentId update in promptMulti() function may cause token loss by transferring to address(0)
findings.why: The loop caches agentTba but never assigns prevAgentId = agentId, so the cache is stale and safeTransferFrom can send to an uninitialised address(0) destination; it is a caching/ordering mistake, not reentrancy or overflow.

findings.title: Attacker can prevent user from executing application registered through initFromToken() in AgentFactoryV4
findings.why: An attacker front-creates the Uniswap pair so `require(factory.getPair(tokenAddr, assetToken) == address(0), "pool already exists")` always reverts, permanently blocking executeTokenApplication; the harm is griefing/denial of service.

findings.title: Missing slippage protection on buy and sell
findings.why: sell()/buy() take no minAmountOut and never compare the computed amountOut against a user-supplied bound; the fix is adding a slippage parameter, not reordering a call or guarding a state write.

findings.title: Slippage protection in AgentTax::dcaSell and BondingTax::swapForAsset is calculated at execution time, providing no protection
findings.why: dcaSell derives minOutput from the amount/price read in the same transaction as the swap, so the bound always passes; this is a defective slippage bound, none of the four Quorum shapes.

findings.title: Launched tokens are vulnerable to flashloan attacks forcing premature graduation, allowing reward manipulation
findings.why: unwrapToken has no time restriction so a flashloan can buy, graduate, unwrap and dump atomically; the fix is adding a delay to the graduation lifecycle, not guarding an external call against re-entry.

findings.title: Division in Bonding.sol._openTradingOnUniswap() results in an incorrect lpSupply, higher vaultSupply, and dust AgentTokens getting locked in FPair
findings.why: tokenBalance / (10 ** decimals()) truncates the remainder before AgentToken.initialize multiplies it back, so lpSupply is understated; that is truncation loss under 0.8 checked math, explicitly not wrapping arithmetic.

findings.title: BondingTax has invalid slippage implementation
findings.why: minOutput is a percentage of router.getAmountsOut() fetched at execution time, i.e. of the very spot price the swap executes at, so the swapExactTokensForTokens bound can never bind.

findings.title: amountOutMin passed in as 0 in AgentToken::_swapTax leads to loss of funds due to slippage
findings.why: _swapTax calls swapExactTokensForTokensSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens with a hardcoded amountOutMin of 0, so any sandwich price is accepted; the fix is computing a minimum, a slippage concern.

findings.title: Score in AgentDAO is not an accurate measure and can be artificially inflated by spamming proposals
findings.why: _castVote pushes `scoreOf(account) + 1` for any voter even when the returned weight is 0 and proposal creation is permissionless, so the uptime metric is gameable; the defect is the scoring rule itself.

findings.title: Functions in FERC20 can't be invoked
findings.why: updateMaxTx/excludeFromMaxTx are onlyOwner but the owner is the Bonding contract, which exposes no wrapper, so the privileged setters are unreachable dead code rather than an unguarded write.

findings.title: Missing totalSupply reduction in burnFrom allows supply manipulation (ERC20 Violation)
findings.why: burnFrom decrements _balances[user] and emits Transfer to address(0) but never touches _totalSupply, an ERC20 conformance break; no value leaves the contract against a never-decremented credit, so it is not the accounting-mismatch shape.

findings.title: AgentDAO::_castVote doesn't check the array of votes emitted, which determine the number of battles fought in EloCalculator.sol
findings.why: _updateMaturity decodes `uint8[] memory votes = abi.decode(params, (uint8[]))` and passes it straight to battleElo with no length or value check; the fix is a require on the array length (10 rounds).

findings.title: No slippage protection during adding liquidity to uniswap
findings.why: The IUniswapV2Router02.addLiquidity call passes 0 for both amountAMin and amountBMin, so the deposit accepts any ratio; the fix is supplying non-zero minimums.

findings.title: Removal of a liquidity pool on AgentToken::removeLiquidityPool still incurs taxes on swaps
findings.why: removeLiquidityPool only calls _liquidityPools.remove() while isLiquidityPool also returns true for the immutable uniswapV2Pair, so tax keeps being charged; the fix is clearing uniswapV2Pair in that setter, a logic gap not a missing caller check (it is onlyOwnerOrFactory).

findings.title: VotesUpgradeable::delegate bypasses the addValidator call, leads to a non-validator holding voting power along with loss of rewards
findings.why: The fix is to add a new `delegate` override calling registry.addValidator, but no `delegate` function exists in AgentVeToken.sol or contracts/virtualPersona/ERC20Votes.sol at this commit - it is inherited from the out-of-scope OpenZeppelin VotesUpgradeable.

findings.title: If FFactory::buyTax and / or FFactory::sellTax is set to 0, buy / sell would revert
findings.why: `require(amount > 0, "Nothing to be swapped")` reverts whenever the tax vault balance is zero, and FRouter.buy/sell call swapForAsset unconditionally, so a zero tax bricks all trading; the fix is returning (false, 0) instead of reverting.

findings.title: Elo calculation error
findings.why: battleElo calls Elo.ratingChange(eloB, eloA, result, k) with the player ratings swapped relative to the score argument, so the sign and magnitude apply to the wrong player; a wrong formula, which the unsafe-math shape explicitly excludes.

findings.title: VirtualGenesisDAO.sol:earlyExecute() proposals can be executed two times
findings.why: earlyExecute calls _executeOperations directly, which per its own NatSpec never sets _proposals[proposalId].executed, so a later public execute() runs the same calldata again; the double run is a separate transaction, not re-entry into an unfinished call.

findings.title: Genesis.sol:onGenesisSuccess() users may lose their unclaimed agentTokens if a second launch occurs before they've claimed their rewards from the first
findings.why: The per-user agent-token entitlement is overwritten rather than incremented on a second launch, destroying an unclaimed credit; the bug erases a balance instead of failing to reduce one, the inverse of the accounting-mismatch shape.

findings.title: Lack of maturity check for non-founder users allowing immediate withdrawals
findings.why: withdraw() applies `require(block.timestamp >= matureAt)` only inside `if (sender == founder)`, so every other staker may exit instantly; the missing constraint is an intended lockup rule, not access control over privileged state.

findings.title: Delegation not revoked on withdrawal allows reward and voting power inflation post-maturity
findings.why: withdraw() burns the balance and pushes a balance checkpoint but never calls _delegate(sender, address(0)), leaving a historical delegatee record that getPastDelegates later credits; the fix is an extra state write on exit, not reordering an external call.

findings.title: battleElo is at risk of underflow revert, which may DOS voting
findings.why: `currentRating + eloA - 1000` under pragma ^0.8.20 with no unchecked block reverts rather than wrapping, so the consequence is blocked voting, which fails the unsafe-math requirement of arithmetic that actually wraps.

findings.title: Founder has to double-stake during migration with the initial LP locked in the old veToken
findings.why: migrateAgent creates a new token/LP/veToken and pulls fresh assetToken from the founder while the old AgentVeToken.withdraw initialLock check keeps the original LP locked; the gap is a missing migration path, not any of the four shapes.

findings.title: Using AgentFactory::setAssetToken will lead to loss of funds
findings.why: setAssetToken is already gated by onlyRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE); the harm is that the single global assetToken is read later by withdraw/executeApplication for applications funded in the old token, so it is an admin-config/state-migration hazard, not an unguarded write.

findings.title: Precision loss in priceALast and priceBLast
findings.why: priceALast returns _pool.reserve1 / _pool.reserve0 with no fixed-point scaling so 1.99 truncates to 1; truncation is explicitly excluded from the unsafe-math shape.

findings.title: Incorrect mathematical logic
findings.why: ratingChange decomposes the exponent via n = 800 +/- ratingDiff and repeated square roots instead of computing 10^(ratingDiff/400), so the expected score is simply the wrong formula, not wrapping arithmetic.

findings.title: Imprecise calculations in launchFor() lead to less liquidity be added to the pair via the router
findings.why: `uint256 k = ((K * 10000) / assetRate)` divides before the later multiplication in the liquidity expression, so the result rounds down; a precision-loss ordering issue under checked 0.8 math.

findings.title: Router address validation logic error prevents valid router assignment
findings.why: setRouter is already onlyOwner; the defect is an inverted require(_router == address(0)) validation check, not a missing access-control guard, reentrancy, wrapping arithmetic, or an undecremented balance.

findings.title: Reward token in GaugeFactoryCL can be drained by anyone
findings.why: createGauge is external with no modifier and writes contract-global state (last_gauge, __gauges) while approving and spending the factory's reward token, so the fix is to add access control on the caller.

findings.title: MinterUpgradeable: double-subtracting smNFT burns causes rebase underpayment
findings.why: circulatingBlack subtracts _smNFTBalance from an already-burn-reduced totalSupply, a wrong formula under pragma 0.8.13 (it would revert, not wrap), so it is not unsafe-math.

findings.title: Critical access control flaw: Role removal logic incorrectly grants unauthorized roles
findings.why: removeRole is guarded by onlyBlackMultisig; the bug is that _addressToRoles[user][k] is assigned from the global _roles array instead of the user's own array, a logic error rather than a missing caller check.

findings.title: 1e10 fixed farming reward in GaugeFactoryCL
findings.why: The hardcoded `uint128 reward = 1e10` means a wildly different value per reward-token decimals, which is an explicitly excluded decimals mismatch, not wrapping arithmetic.

findings.title: Logic error in AVM original owner resolution
findings.why: claim_many omits the avm.getOriginalOwner lookup that claim() performs before IERC20(token).transfer, so rewards go to the wrong recipient; no guard, wrapping, or undecremented balance is involved.

findings.title: Griefing attack on GenesisPoolManager.sol::depositNativeToken leading to Denial of Service
findings.why: An attacker front-creates the pair and dusts it so the require(IERC20(nativeToken).balanceOf(pairAddress) == 0) check reverts every legitimate deposit, a griefing DoS rather than any of the four shapes.

findings.title: First liquidity provider can DOS the pool of a stable pair
findings.why: _a = (_x * _y) / 1e18 truncates to zero for tiny amounts, which is precision loss under pragma 0.8.13 and explicitly not unsafe-math; the fix adds a MINIMUM_K check in mint.

findings.title: isGenesis flag is ineffective to control add liquidity flow in RouterV2.addLiquidity()
findings.why: The guard require(!(isGenesis(pair) && totalSupply()==0)) is too weak once any dust LP exists, so the fix is to strengthen the validation condition, not to add reentrancy or caller guards.

findings.title: Function return variable shadowing prevents storage updates in solidity
findings.why: The named return `uint256 rewardRate` shadows the storage variable so the storage write never happens; the function is already onlyDistribution and nonReentrant.

findings.title: Zero-receiver fund burn
findings.why: _swap sends output to routes[i].receiver (unset, address(0)) and ignores its own `_to` parameter, a wrong-destination logic bug, not a guard, wrapping, or balance-decrement issue.

findings.title: ERC-2612 permit front-running in RouterV2 enables DoS of liquidity operations
findings.why: An attacker replays the user's signature directly on IBaseV1Pair(pair).permit so the unconditional permit call in removeLiquidityWithPermit reverts; the fix is try/catch around a front-runnable call.

findings.title: Incorrect function call in BribeFactoryV3 recoverERC20AndUpdateData
findings.why: The fix is to call IBribe.recoverERC20AndUpdateData instead of IBribe.emergencyRecoverERC20; the function where the fix belongs holds no balance of its own, so it is not the classic pay-out-without-decrement shape.

findings.title: Epoch voting restrictions bypassed via deposit_for() for blacklisted/non-whitelisted tokenIDs
findings.why: poke lacks the epoch/whitelist checks that vote() enforces, letting vote weight be recast after the epoch; it writes per-tokenId vote state the caller owns, not privileged config.

findings.title: EIP-712 domain type hash mismatch breaks signature-based delegation
findings.why: DOMAIN_TYPEHASH omits the `string version` field that delegateBySig's abi.encode of the domain separator supplies, so every ecrecover digest is wrong.

findings.title: Checkpoints are incorrectly cleared during transferFrom
findings.why: The in-place srcRepNew swap-and-pop loop runs after _removeTokenFrom has zeroed the owner, so ownerOfFn(tId) != srcRep is always true and the checkpoint array is wiped; it is a loop logic error, not wrapping arithmetic.

findings.title: L2Governor.execute() accepts Expired / Defeated proposals, attacker front-runs BlackGovernor nudge()
findings.why: The require in execute permits ProposalState.Defeated and .Expired alongside .Succeeded, so the fix narrows a state check; execute writes proposal state that any caller is meant to advance, not privileged config.

findings.title: getVotes inside the BlackGovernor incorrectly provides block.number instead of block.timestamp
findings.why: _proposal passes block.number - 1 into getVotes, which expects a timestamp, a unit mix-up in a threshold check rather than wrapping arithmetic or a missing guard.

findings.title: Users can cast their votes multiple times for the proposal by transferring their nfts and then voting again
findings.why: _castVote tracks hasVoted per account and never marks the tokenIds used, so transferring the NFT and voting from a new address double-counts weight; no external call ordering or balance decrement is at issue.

findings.title: Status does not update inside the BlackGovernor leading to complete distribution of nudge functionality
findings.why: The local `ProposalState status = state(proposalId)` in execute shadows the public `status` storage variable, which therefore stays Pending for Minter.nudge(); it is a shadowing bug, not a missing access-control guard.

findings.title: Quorum does not include the againstVotes leading to emissions rate staying the same even if it should decrease
findings.why: _quorumReached compares quorum() against forVotes + abstainVotes only, omitting againstVotes; it is a view function with a wrong tally formula, not any of the four shapes.

findings.title: getsmNFTPastVotes incorrectly checks for Voting Power leading to some NFTs incorrectly being eligible to vote
findings.why: getsmNFTPastVotes reads the current locked[tId].isSMNFT flag while summing balances at a past timestamp, a historical-state logic error in a view function.

findings.title: Governance emission adjustment ignored when weekly emission above tail threshold
findings.why: update_period applies tailEmissionRate only inside the `if (_weekly < TAIL_START)` branch, so the DAO vote is ignored above the threshold; it is a branching-condition logic error.

findings.title: Governance deadlock potential in BlackGovernor.sol due to quorum mismatch
findings.why: quorum() derives its target from the monotonically increasing smNFTBalance while proposalThreshold uses total veBLACK power, a design mismatch in a view function with no state write, call, or wrapping arithmetic.

findings.title: Same heartbeat for multiple price feeds is vulnerable
findings.why: The staleness check `block.timestamp - updatedAt_ > allowedPriceUpdateDelay` applies one global delay to every Chainlink aggregator, an oracle freshness configuration flaw, not reentrancy, wrapping math, or an unguarded privileged write.

findings.title: Inconsistent balance accounting in stETH deposits leads to DOS of core functions and reward loss
findings.why: supply() credits depositPool.deposited and lastUnderlyingBalance with the requested amount_ rather than the realized stETH balance delta, a rebasing-token integration flaw whose underflow reverts under the 0.8.20 pragma instead of wrapping.

findings.title: Protocol doesn't properly handle Aave Pool changes
findings.why: setAavePool is onlyOwner so it is not an unguarded state write; the defect is that it rewrites `aavePool` without revoking the old allowance or approving the new pool, leaving Aave-strategy flows unusable.

findings.title: Yield withdrawal blocked by zero reward early return
findings.why: The `if (rewards_ == 0) return;` early exit in distributeRewards skips the lastUnderlyingBalance refresh so post-maxEndTime yield is never recognized, a control-flow/business-logic defect with no external-call ordering, wrapping math, or missing access control.

findings.title: Assets deposited before calculating shares amount to mint will cause users to mint less shares
findings.why: deposit() calls IVotingEscrow(votingEscrow).deposit_for before calculateShares(amount), so totalAssets() already includes the depositor's own funds when the share ratio is taken — a mis-ordered computation in a nonReentrant function, not a re-enterable external call, an unguarded privileged write, or arithmetic that wraps under pragma 0.8.13.

findings.title: CLFactory ignores dynamic fees above 10% and silently falls back to default
findings.why: getSwapFee returns tickSpacingToFee whenever the module reports fee > 100_000 instead of reverting; it is a view function with a missing range check, so no state is written, nothing re-enters, and nothing wraps.

findings.title: Users emergency withdrawing will lose all past accrued rewards
findings.why: emergencyWithdraw() zeroes _balances[msg.sender] without the updateReward modifier, so earned() afterwards multiplies a zero balance and the accrual is silently dropped — lost rewards from a missing checkpoint, not a double payout, a wrap, or a re-enterable ordering (the function is nonReentrant).

findings.title: First depositor attack possible through multiple attack paths because the deposit function does not check 0 shares received
findings.why: deposit() mints calculateShares(amount) with no require(shares > 0), so a donation-inflated totalAssets() divisor rounds the victim's shares down to zero — a missing zero-share check plus rounding, explicitly not wrapping arithmetic under pragma 0.8.13.

findings.title: Dust vote on one pool prevents poke()
findings.why: require(_poolWeight != 0, "ZV") in _vote reverts once a 1 wei vote weight rounds to zero against a decayed balance, permanently bricking poke() for that veNFT — a liveness failure, not a wrap, an unguarded write, or a re-entered call.

findings.title: Rollover rewards are permanently lost due to flawed rewardRate calculation
findings.why: notifyRewardAmount sets rewardRate = rewardAmount / epochTimeRemaining while syncing rewardReserve to totalRewardAmount = rewardAmount + clPool.rollover(), so the rate omits the rollover — a wrong formula, which the unsafe-math shape explicitly excludes.

findings.title: ClaimFees steals staking rewards
findings.why: _claimFees sets claimed0/claimed1 to IERC20(token).balanceOf(address(this)) after clPool.collectFees() and forwards the whole sweep to internal_bribe, so notified staking rewards go out too; nothing is a repeatedly payable storage credit, so it is not the accounting-mismatch shape.

findings.title: Claiming rewards in GovernanceHYBR will always revert
findings.why: claimRewards decodes IVoter(voter).poolVote(veTokenId) as address[] while VoterV3's auto-generated getter for mapping(uint256 => address[]) requires an index, so the call always reverts — an ABI/interface mismatch, not any of the four shapes.

findings.title: Incorrect voting power calculation when create_lock and increase_amount are called in the same transaction
findings.why: _checkpoint unconditionally does user_point_epoch[_tokenId] + 1 and appends a new point even when the previous point has the same block.timestamp, so balanceOfNFT reads the stale point — a history-bookkeeping bug, not wrapping arithmetic or a missing access check.

findings.title: CL gauge accepts unverified pools, allowing malicious pool to brick distribution
findings.why: _createGauge hardcodes isPair = true for _gaugeType == 1 instead of verifying the pool came from the CL factory, so the missing input validation lets a fake pool in; the state it writes (gauges/isCLGauge) is the factory's intended permissionless registration, not privileged config like owner, fee, or oracle.

findings.title: Chained signature with checkpoint usage disabled can bypass all checkpointer validation
findings.why: recover() only enters the checkpointer block when signatureFlag & 0x40 is set, so a chained signature with that bit cleared leaves _checkpointer and snapshot.imageHash zero and every later snapshot check passes — a signature-validation bypass, not reentrancy, an unguarded state write, or wrapping arithmetic.

findings.title: Partial signature replay/frontrunning attack on session calls
findings.why: hashCallWithReplayProtection hashes only (chainid, space, nonce, callIdx, hashCall) per call, so when a BEHAVIOR_REVERT_ON_ERROR batch reverts and un-consumes the nonce a subset of the per-call signatures can be replayed — a signature-binding/replay defect.

findings.title: Session signatures replay across wallets due to missing wallet binding
findings.why: hashCallWithReplayProtection omits the wallet address from the signed preimage, so a session signature valid for wallet A is accepted by any sibling wallet sharing the image hash and nonce — cross-wallet signature replay, none of the four shapes.

findings.title: Static signatures bound to caller revert under ERC-4337, causing DoS
findings.why: validateUserOp's external self-call this.isValidSignature(...) makes msg.sender inside BaseAuth.signatureValidation the wallet rather than the EntryPoint, so caller-bound static signatures always revert with InvalidStaticSignatureWrongCaller — a liveness break, with no state write, wrap, or exploitable re-entry.

findings.title: BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature returns a constant instead of signer image hash, breaking sapient signer flows
findings.why: recoverSapientSignature returns the literal bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of the signer's imageHash required by ISapient, so BaseSig.recoverBranch builds the wrong sapient leaf — an interface-contract violation, not reentrancy, a missing access check, a wrap, or a double-paid balance.

findings.title: Factory deploy reverts instead of returning address when account already exists
findings.why: deploy()'s create2 returns address(0) on CreateCollision and the function reverts with DeployFailed rather than returning the existing wallet, so an attacker front-running the deployment griefs ERC-4337 flows — a liveness/compatibility break, not one of the four shapes.

findings.title: Oracle Data Corruption via Storage Key Collision
findings.why: The bug is a raw storage-slot derivation collision (`sstore(token, c)` for Counts versus `sstore(or(shl(32,token),index), snapshot)` for Snapshot) letting one token's metadata overwrite another's snapshot, which is neither an external call ordering issue, a missing access-control check on privileged config, an arithmetic wrap, nor a never-decremented balance.

findings.title: TWAMM Instant Orders Can Steal Historical Rewards
findings.why: When `block.timestamp == startTime` the else-branch skips `_updateTime(poolId, startTime, ...)` so `rewardRatesBeforeSlot[startTime]` stays uninitialized at 0 — a missing state initialization in normal control flow, not a reentrant call, a privileged-state write, an arithmetic wrap (the `unchecked` subtraction is the intended cumulative-difference pattern), or a never-decremented balance.

findings.title: Wrong rounding direction in DurationRemaining leads to value loss from TWAMM extension and Temporarily Freezing of a Pool
findings.why: `computeAmountFromSaleRate({saleRate: saleRate, duration: durationRemaining, roundUp: true})` for `remainingSellAmount` rounds in the user's favour by 1 wei per cancellation, which is a rounding-direction error and explicitly excluded from unsafe-math (nothing wraps; the pragma is >=0.8.30).

findings.title: Router does not check if Exact Out Single Swap was partial leading to unexpected results for the users
findings.why: The single-swap branch only checks `amountCalculated < calculatedAmountThreshold` and never asserts the exact-out leg was fully filled, a missing user-protection/slippage check rather than a reentrancy, access-control, wrapping-arithmetic or double-payout balance issue.

findings.title: Unchecked approve() return causes permanent fund loss in UDA.sol
findings.why: initialize() calls HTLC(_addressHTLC).token().approve(_addressHTLC, amount) and discards the boolean return, so a non-standard ERC20 like USDT that returns false leaves allowance at 0 — a token-integration defect (fix is safeApprove), not reentrancy, an unguarded privileged write, wrapping arithmetic under pragma 0.8.28, or a never-decremented balance.

findings.title: Attacker can steal JackpotTicketNFT's from JackpotBridgeManager.sol
findings.why: _bridgeFunds performs `_bridgeDetails.to.call(_bridgeDetails.data)` with a fully user-controlled target and calldata and no whitelist, so the manager can be made to call safeTransferFrom on the NFT it custodies; the fix is to validate the call target, not to reorder or guard a state write.

findings.title: Unoptimized subset matches counting implementation will exceed tx gas limit on base chain
findings.why: The nested loop over `_tracker.bonusballMax` x `normalTiers` regenerates Combinations.generateSubsets every iteration, pushing settlement past Base's 25M gas limit so the entropy callback can never land — a gas-exhaustion DoS, not reentrancy, an unguarded write, wrapping math or a double-paid balance.

findings.title: LP pool cap may be exceeded on drawing settlement
findings.why: processDrawingSettlement computes newLPValue = postDrawLpValue + pendingDeposits - withdrawalsInUSDC without re-applying the lpPoolCap/governancePoolCap check, so LP growth from a winner-less draw breaks the cap invariant; that is a missing invariant, not overflow, missing access control (it is onlyJackpot), reentrancy or an unreduced credit.

findings.title: Global Variable Manipulation During Active Draw Alters End Result
findings.why: setProtocolFee (and the sibling setters for referralFee, payoutCalculator and entropy) writes privileged state but is already gated by onlyOwner, so this is an admin-timing/trust flaw — the parameter is read during settlement of an already-open draw — not an unguarded state write.

findings.title: Incorrect ticket price reference in JackpotBridgeManager causes user overpayment after price updates
findings.why: buyTickets reads Jackpot's current global `ticketPrice` instead of the frozen per-drawing price, so after a price update it pulls/approves the wrong amount (funds stranded on a raise, insufficient-approval revert on a cut) — a wrong-source-of-truth logic bug, not wrapping arithmetic or a reentrancy ordering issue.

findings.title: Deliberately increasing liquidity can DoS updates to the protocol's governance parameters
findings.why: setLPPoolCap reverts with InvalidLPPoolCap whenever the new cap is below lpPoolTotal + pendingDeposits, so an LP front-running with a deposit permanently blocks governance parameter changes — a griefing/DoS revert, with access control (onlyJackpot) present and no arithmetic wrap involved.

findings.title: lpEarnings generated in emergency mode become stuck on the contract
findings.why: _payReferrersWinnings keeps crediting `drawingState[currentDrawingId].lpEarnings` while emergency mode blocks runJackpot from ever settling that drawing, so the USDC is trapped rather than double-paid — the inverse of an accounting-mismatch, and no external call ordering or overflow is implicated.

findings.title: Randomness can be exploited in some cases
findings.why: _getScaledRandomness derives the normal balls and the bonus ball from the same entropy seed, so when normalBallMax equals bonusballMax the bonus ball always falls inside the normal set and players can cut their odds ~6x — a randomness-derivation weakness, not reentrancy, an unguarded write, wrapping math or a double-spendable credit.

findings.title: Changes to Pyth entropy provider used by ScaledEntropyProvider allow attacker to fix jackpot result
findings.why: _storePendingRequest keys `pending` by the Pyth sequence number alone, which is only unique per entropy provider, so after setEntropyProvider an attacker's stale setRequests survive at the same sequence and dictate the drawn numbers; the fix is to key the mapping by provider as well, not to guard a reentrant call or fix arithmetic.

findings.title: Changing Entropy Provider During Active Drawing Causes Permanent Protocol Lock and Callback Failure
findings.why: setEntropy overwrites the `entropy` address with no check that a drawing is mid-flight, so the pending callback from the old provider is rejected by onlyEntropy and settlement locks — an admin-timing logic flaw on a function that already has onlyOwner, so not an unguarded state write.

findings.title: Changing Payout Calculator During Active Drawing Causes Loss of Unclaimed Winnings
findings.why: setPayoutCalculator swaps the `payoutCalculator` reference with no active-drawing guard, so claimWinnings later queries a calculator that holds no tier data for past drawings and unclaimed prizes evaporate; the function is onlyOwner, so this is admin/logic risk rather than an unguarded state write.

findings.title: Minimum Reward-Per-Hour Validation Applied to Gross Instead of Net Amount
findings.why: The check `(newCampaign.amount * HOUR) / newCampaign.duration < rewardTokenMinAmount` runs before `_computeFees` overwrites `newCampaign.amount` with the net amount, so the guard validates the wrong value — a validation-ordering flaw with no wrapping arithmetic (pragma ^0.8.17, no `unchecked`), no missing access control, and no repeated payout.

findings.title: Improper Error Handling of onClaim Callback in _claim Function
findings.why: The `try IClaimRecipient(recipient).onClaim(...) { if (callbackSuccess != CALLBACK_SUCCESS) revert ... } catch {}` puts the revert inside the success handler and swallows genuine failures; `_claim` is `nonReentrant` and the claimed amount is written before the transfer, so this is callback error-handling logic, not reentrancy.

findings.title: Multi-step campaign overrides are anchored to the original campaign, making later overrides impossible
findings.why: `overrideCampaign` validates `newCampaign.startTimestamp != _campaign.startTimestamp && block.timestamp > _campaign.startTimestamp` against the original `campaignList` entry instead of the latest `campaignOverrides` entry, a wrong-baseline logic error — the function is gated by `_isValidOperator(_campaign.creator)`, makes no external call, and involves no wrapping arithmetic or unreduced balance.

findings.title: Missing Authorization Check Allows Unauthorized Fund Withdrawal
findings.why: `withdraw`/`redeem` pass an arbitrary `owner` into `_withdraw`, which calls `_shareToken.spendSelfAllowance(owner, shares)` with no `msg.sender == owner` or `allowance[owner][msg.sender]` check — a missing caller-authorization check on another user's funds, not a write to privileged protocol state such as owner/fee/rate/oracle/pause.

findings.title: The unregistering of vaults can be DoSed by a malicious user
findings.why: The `IERC20(asset).balanceOf(vaultAddress) != 0` guard and the dust-sensitive metrics checks in `unregisterVault` let anyone donate 1 wei to permanently revert the owner-only call, which is griefing/DoS rather than reentrancy, missing access control (it is `onlyOwner`), arithmetic wrapping, or a double-paid balance.

findings.title: Stale Redemption Liabilities Lead to Leveraged Losses for Remaining Shareholders and Potential Denial of Service
findings.why: `assets = _convertToAssets(shares, Math.Rounding.Floor)` permanently locks the price-per-share into `claimableRedeemAssets[controller]` with no expiry or repricing, a design/economic-logic issue about when the PPS is fixed, not an external-call ordering bug, a privileged-state write, an arithmetic wrap, or a balance that is credited and never debited.

findings.title: fulfillRedeem may corrupt share price and allow over-redemption of assets
findings.why: `totalAssets()` clamps `balance - reservedAssets` at zero, so once `claimableRedeemAssets` exceeds the vault's own balance the liability silently stops being subtracted and the share price inflates — an unaccounted-liability formula error, not a wrapping-arithmetic bug (pragma ^0.8.30, the clamp is an explicit condition) nor a balance that is never reduced.
